clue.text: Musician heading off to lend a hand

indicators.note: the musician's head, its first letter, goes away

parts.note: a bassist plays the bass guitar or double bass

explanation.surface: A player sets off to help out a fellow musician.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to help, which is what lending a hand idiomatically means.

clue.text: Making a collection of Schubert's choral work

definitions.meaning: second sense: Schubert wrote a Mass in G major, whose title run together spells the word

explanation.walkthrough: Read the title 'a Mass in G' as one run of letters and the choral work becomes a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or accumulate, and Schubert's Mass in G is a real choral setting.

clue.text: Settled with bribe, as some paper might be?

definitions.meaning: first sense: a debt or account ... is paid off
second sense: to square someone is to bribe or fix them
third sense: graph paper is printed ..., ruled in a grid

explanation.walkthrough: Three separate senses of one past participle: paid up, bought off, and ruled in a grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Squared covers settling an account, bribing an official, and the grid ruling on graph paper.

clue.text: If ordered, jet can support boat that's lying below

indicators.note: in a down clue the reworked letters sit underneath and so hold up the boat

parts.note: a sub is a submarine, a boat in naval usage

indicators.note: putting the letters of jet can in a fresh order gives a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Instructions for loading a jet ski onto a boat moored beneath.
explanation.definitionFit: Subjacent is a formal word for situated underneath or lower down.

clue.text: Jenny Gold, the tax inspector

parts.note: a jenny is a female donkey, jokingly an ass with the feminine ending -ess, like lioness
or is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: A woman called Jenny Gold works as the revenue's inspector.
explanation.walkthrough: Jenny looks like a first name; it is a she-donkey, made into a mock feminine of ass.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessor fixes the value of property or income for taxation purposes.

clue.text: One who detected more suffering with shell-shock

indicators.note: the letters are in a bad way, so they come out jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone is suffering more because of shell-shock from the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Conan Doyle's fictional detective is the most famous sleuth of all, so he is the one who detected.

clue.text: Doctor finally prescribes exercise: running up racecourse

indicators.note: in a down clue the letters run upwards, so they read in reverse

parts.note: MO is a medical officer

indicators.note: only the last letter of prescribes is taken

parts.note: the last letter of prescribes
PE is physical education

explanation.surface: A doctor orders exercise: jogging up a racecourse.
explanation.walkthrough: Epsom Downs, in Surrey, is the English racecourse where the Derby is run.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom is the home of the Derby, one of the best-known horse-racing venues in England.

clue.text: Liberal put into lampoon gets cross

indicators.note: the liberal is placed inside the lampoon

parts.note: a satire mocks its target, as a lampoon does

explanation.surface: A Liberal politician mocked in a lampoon becomes angry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like an adjective for anger; it is the noun, a diagonal cross as on the Scottish flag.
explanation.definitionFit: A saltire is an X-shaped heraldic cross, the St Andrew's cross of Scotland.

clue.text: Give up job, or take it back?

definitions.meaning: first sense: to quit a post
second sense: read as ..., to sign up again and so take the post back

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the word as re-sign, signing on again; the question mark flags that pun.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to step down from employment, while re-signing a contract takes the position back.

clue.text: In a temper when vessel, fuel transport, is given lousy refit

parts.note: a can is a container, a vessel for liquid
a tanker carries oil or petrol

indicators.note: the word lousy is fitted together again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fumes because their ship, an oil tanker, got a shoddy refit.
explanation.definitionFit: Cantankerously means in a bad-tempered, quarrelsome way, an adverb phrase like the definition.

clue.text: Outline a foolish tax

parts.note: taken as written
dumb is stupid, chiefly in American use
a rate is a local tax

explanation.surface: Describe in brief a tax that is silly.
explanation.walkthrough: Rates were the British local property tax before council tax.
explanation.definitionFit: To adumbrate is to sketch or indicate in broad strokes, giving only a faint outline.

clue.text: 6's might revive old sailors

definitions.meaning: first sense: Epsom (6 down) ... are a tonic and purgative that may perk one up
second sense: an old salt is a seasoned sailor

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference points to 6 down, a racecourse; the town also gave its name to Epsom salts.
explanation.definitionFit: Epsom salts are magnesium sulphate taken as a remedy, and experienced seamen are called old salts.

clue.text: Housekeeper is watchful when old boy's away

indicators.note: the old boy is gone, so his letters leave the word

parts.note: observant means alert and attentive
OB is a former pupil, an old boy; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: The housekeeper keeps a sharp eye out whenever the master is absent.
explanation.definitionFit: A housekeeper is a domestic employee, so a kind of servant.

clue.text: You'll see one mingle with mass self-destructively

definitions.text: You'll see one mingle with mass self-destructively

indicators.note: the word mingle wrecks itself, so its letters break up and regroup

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Watch one join the crowd heading over the cliff to its doom.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: lemmings are popularly said to mingle in a mass and hurl themselves to their deaths.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore has the rodent migrating in hordes and plunging off cliffs, a byword for suicidal conformity.

clue.text: Give a reminder, say, and press to be paid back

indicators.note: paying back runs the letters the other way, so they read in reverse

parts.note: eg means for example
to dun is to press a debtor for payment

explanation.surface: Remind a debtor, and lean on them until the money comes back.
explanation.walkthrough: The debt-collecting surface suits dun, which means to demand payment.
explanation.definitionFit: A nudge is a gentle prompt, so to nudge someone is to jog their memory.

clue.text: Offered a pound, journalist gave soft laugh

indicators.note: the pound is offered to the journalist, so it comes first, handed to the editor

parts.note: nicker is British slang for a pound sterling
ED is an editor

explanation.surface: Handed a pound as a bribe, the reporter gave a quiet chuckle.
explanation.walkthrough: Nicker is slang for a pound coin; as a verb it also means to snigger or whinny softly.
explanation.definitionFit: To nicker is to give a low, half-suppressed laugh, like a snigger.

clue.text: Part of the State Carriages employed at Sandringham?

definitions.text: Part of the State Carriages employed at Sandringham?

indicators.note: the letters are a portion of the words that follow

parts.note: the run thE STATE CARriages holds the two words, spanning the joins

explanation.surface: Which state coaches does the royal household use at Sandringham?
explanation.walkthrough: Sandringham, the royal residence in Norfolk, is an estate, so its cars are estate cars; the word Carriages serves both the hidden run and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An estate car is a station wagon, and Sandringham is literally a country estate.

clue.text: Little girl and two boys given away

parts.note: Bet is a short form of Elizabeth
Ray and Ed are two boys' names

explanation.surface: A small girl and two boys are put up for adoption.
explanation.definitionFit: Betrayed means revealed or let slip, as a secret is given away.

clue.text: Canines one would sacrifice if in real want?

definitions.text: one would sacrifice if in real want?
definitions.meaning: second sense: to give one's ... for something is to want it desperately

explanation.walkthrough: The second half rests on the idiom 'I'd give my eye teeth for that', meaning to long for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The upper canine teeth are called eye teeth, and the idiom offers them up as a great sacrifice.

clue.text: Beast can eat remains — Mark makes modest assumption

indicators.note: the beast is able to swallow what follows, taking it inside

parts.note: a yak is a Tibetan ox
ash is what is left after burning
M is short for mark, the old German currency

explanation.surface: An animal can graze on scraps, and someone called Mark draws a humble conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assumption' looks like a guess; here it is something put on, a garment assumed.
explanation.definitionFit: A yashmak is the veil worn by some Muslim women for modesty, so it is a garment assumed modestly.

clue.text: Initially terrible pain that may show on one's face

definitions.text: that may show on one's face
definitions.note: a noun phrase: the thing that may be seen on a face

indicators.note: only the opening letter of terrible is used

parts.note: the first letter of terrible
an ache is a dull pain

explanation.surface: A sudden agony that shows in a grimace.
explanation.walkthrough: Tache is British slang for a moustache.
explanation.definitionFit: A tache is a moustache, which naturally appears on a man's upper lip.

clue.text: Here's one blooming winner doing without drug!

indicators.note: the champion has to manage without the drug, which is removed

parts.note: a champion is a winner
H is slang for heroin

explanation.surface: A cheer for a winner who competes clean, free of drugs!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blooming' looks like a mild British oath; it means flowering.
explanation.definitionFit: Campion is a wild flower of the pink family, a plant that blooms.

clue.text: Hot rich bread left out

indicators.note: the left is left out, so one of its letters goes

parts.note: stollen is a rich German fruit loaf eaten at Christmas

explanation.surface: Warm, rich bread left out to cool.
explanation.definitionFit: Hot is slang for stolen goods, recently stolen and so risky to handle.

clue.text: This enabled soldiers to undertake dangerous operation at the front

definitions.text: This enabled soldiers to undertake dangerous operation at the front

indicators.note: the front of each word, its first letter, is taken

parts.words: This enabled soldiers to undertake dangerous operation
parts.note: the first letters of these seven words, read in order

explanation.surface: A device that let troops attempt risky work in the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines too: Roman legionaries locked shields overhead in a testudo to advance on walls under fire.
explanation.definitionFit: The testudo, Latin for tortoise, was a protective shield formation for assaulting fortifications.

clue.text: Peace-keepers acted and solved knotty problem

parts.note: the UN, United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces
did means performed or acted

explanation.surface: The peacekeepers took action and settled a thorny dispute.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knotty problem' sounds figurative, but it is literal: an actual knot was undone.
explanation.definitionFit: Undid means untied, which literally solves a knot.

clue.text: Bishop withdrawing pardon, just the one time

indicators.note: the word draws back, read from the end
of the two letters for time, only one is kept

parts.note: remittal is remission, a pardon of a penalty or debt

explanation.surface: A bishop retracts his absolution, allowing it only this once.
explanation.walkthrough: Hugh Latimer was a Protestant Bishop of Worcester, burned at Oxford in 1555.
explanation.definitionFit: Latimer, the English Reformation martyr, held the see of Worcester as a bishop.

clue.text: With crippling injury, medal's lost

indicators.note: the medal is lost, its letters scattered into a new order

parts.note: medal's is read as medal is, so only the word medal gives letters

explanation.surface: A war hero, badly wounded, has lost the decoration too.
explanation.definitionFit: Lamed means made lame, crippled by an injury to the leg.

clue.text: Talk at length with a faculty, even though unknown

parts.note: speech is one of the human faculties
if can mean although, as in 'pleasant if dull'
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: Someone holds forth with an academic department despite being an unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Faculty' looks like a university department; it is a mental power.
explanation.definitionFit: To speechify is to make long, pompous speeches, holding forth tediously.

clue.text: With which to observe what's barely visible?

definitions.text: With which to observe what's barely visible?

parts.words: With which to observe what's barely visible?
parts.note: barely reads as without clothes as well as only just, so the instrument for faint sights is the uncovered eye

explanation.walkthrough: Something barely visible sounds like a faint star; read barely as unclothed and it is the eye that sees it.
explanation.definitionFit: The unaided eye, without telescope or microscope, is how astronomers describe observing faint objects.

clue.text: Dancer awkwardly stretched neck

indicators.note: an awkward dancer lands in the wrong places, signalling the jumble

explanation.surface: A clumsy ballerina strained her neck.
explanation.definitionFit: Craned means stretched the neck to see, as a crane bird extends its long neck.
